title: PD-L1 mediates M1 polarization of macrophages via the AIM2/IL-18/STAT1 signaling axis during sepsis.
authors: Yang, Guomei; Ao, Luoquan; Zhao, Qing; Hu, Chengyi; Wu, Xiaofeng; Yao, Mengwei; Yuan, Mu; Jin, Tong; Wan, Weijun; Chen, Quan; Yuan, Yuchuan; Xu, Xiang; Tian, Lixing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脓毒症中PD-L1通过AIM2/IL-18/STAT1轴调控巨噬细胞M1极化，属于免疫信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模内容，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis, a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host responses to infection, has emerged as a leading cause of mortality in ICU patients. Macrophages, crucial effector cells in innate immunity, play pivotal regulatory roles in sepsis pathogenesis. While Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), a key immune checkpoint molecule, is traditionally believed to exert immunosuppressive effects through membrane anchoring, its involvement in macrophage polarization during sepsis remains unclear. This study investigated the spatial distribution of PD-L1 in macrophages and its regulatory effects on inflammatory responses during sepsis. METHODS: This study investigated PD-L1's regulatory role in macrophage polarization through RNA sequencing, Immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, molecular docking, and site-directed mutagenesis, with preliminary validation in C57BL/6 mice. RESULTS: Using GEO database analysis combined with qRT-PCR and Western blotting, we confirmed elevated PD-L1 expression in sepsis and M1-polarized macrophages. Laser scanning confocal microscopy demonstrated dual localization of PD-L1, appearing both on the plasma membrane and intracellularly within M1 macrophages. RNA sequencing revealed PD-L1's promotion of M1 polarization through enhanced AIM2 expression in the NOD-like receptor pathway. Integrated analyses employing mass spectrometry, molecular docking, site-directed mutagenesis, and Western blotting demonstrated PD-L1 binding to AIM2, which augmented expression of downstream effector molecules (IL-18 and IFN-gamma) and potentiated STAT1 activation. Silencing AIM2 by siRNA or IL-18 antagonism reversed PD-L1-induced M1 markers (IL-27, IL-6, iNOS/NO). PD-L1 was further shown to exacerbate pathological progression in septic mouse models. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that sepsis-induced PD-L1 overexpression in macrophages exacerbates pathological progression by upregulating AIM2 expression, binding to AIM2 to enhance IL-18 production, which activates STAT1 to drive M1 polarization.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症（sepsis）是一种由宿主对感染反应失调引起的危及生命的器官功能障碍，已成为ICU患者死亡的主要原因。巨噬细胞作为先天免疫中的关键效应细胞，在脓毒症发病机制中发挥重要调控作用。程序性死亡配体1（PD-L1）作为一种关键免疫检查点分子，传统上被认为通过膜锚定发挥免疫抑制作用，但其在脓毒症期间巨噬细胞极化中的作用仍不清楚。本研究探讨了脓毒症期间PD-L1在巨噬细胞中的空间分布及其对炎症反应的调控作用。方法：本研究通过RNA测序、免疫沉淀-质谱联用、分子对接和定点突变技术，探讨了PD-L1在巨噬细胞极化中的调控作用，并在C57BL/6小鼠中进行了初步验证。结果：通过GEO数据库分析结合qRT-PCR和Western blotting，我们确认了脓毒症和M1极化巨噬细胞中PD-L1表达升高。激光扫描共聚焦显微镜显示PD-L1在M1巨噬细胞中具有双重定位，既出现在质膜上，也出现在细胞内。RNA测序揭示PD-L1通过增强NOD样受体通路中的AIM2表达促进M1极化。综合质谱、分子对接、定点突变和Western blotting分析表明，PD-L1与AIM2结合，增强了下游效应分子（IL-18和IFN-γ）的表达，并增强了STAT1的激活。通过siRNA沉默AIM2或IL-18拮抗作用可逆转PD-L1诱导的M1标志物（IL-27、IL-6、iNOS/NO）。进一步研究表明，PD-L1加剧了脓毒症小鼠模型的病理进展。结论：我们的研究表明，脓毒症诱导的巨噬细胞中PD-L1过表达通过上调AIM2表达、与AIM2结合增强IL-18产生，进而激活STAT1驱动M1极化，从而加剧病理进展。
